Background

The Green Climate Fund (GCF) is the world's largest dedicated climate fund and supports developing countries in pursuing low-emission and climate-resilient development pathways. The Accreditation and Entity Relations Unit (AERU) within the Department of Investment Services supports Accredited Entities (AEs) throughout the accreditation lifecycle and partnership journey with GCF. This includes onboarding newly accredited entities, institution-level reporting under the Monitoring and Accountability Framework (MAF), advisory and capacity-building services, particularly for Direct Access Entities (DAEs), communications, knowledge management, and support for institution-level compliance and partnership obligations.

Under the Revised Accreditation Framework, GCF is strengthening the application of specialized fiduciary standards across relevant accreditation and programming processes. As part of this effort, most SFS-related screening requirements are being operationalized within the Concept Note (CN), Funding Proposal (FP), and Project Preparation Facility (PPF) processes.

The Secretariat seeks to recruit a Specialized Fiduciary Standards Operations and Process Consultant to provide substantive operational, analytical, and process-design support for this institutional progression. The consultant will join the Department of Investment Services at GCF headquarters in Songdo, Republic of Korea. The assignment is for an initial period of 12 months.
Role

The Consultant will support the translation of approved specialized fiduciary standards requirements into coherent, implementation-ready processes for programming stage. The Consultant will undertake analysis of current procedures and system arrangements, identify gaps and dependencies, assist in developing proposed operating solutions, and coordinate the preparation of process documents, tools, requirements, and implementation controls for review and approval by the designated GCF authorities.

The Consultant will provide administrative as well as analytical support on fiduciary standards and related operational processes; coordinate cross-functional work with Regional Teams, the Office of the Chief Investment Officer, the Department of Information Technology, and other relevant stakeholders; and facilitate the implementation of agreed actions. The Consultant will report to the Fiduciary Advisory Principal and work under the overall oversight of the Head of the Accreditation and Entity Relations Unit.
Duties and responsibilities
The Consultant will be accountable for the quality and timely delivery of assigned outputs on specialized fiduciary standards and will be responsible for:
A. Process Analysis and Operational Framework Development
Support drafting, formatting, cross-referencing, consolidation of comments, change logging, and version control of proposed SOP and process-flow amendments.
Maintain controlled records showing the status and implementation of approved SOP and process-flow changes.
Assist in developing proposed end-to-end operating arrangements for specialized fiduciary standards

Prepare drafts and proposed amendments to standard operating procedures, process flowcharts, checklists, guidance notes, templates, decision records, and reviewer tools, ensuring that documents are internally consistent.
Analyze recurring implementation issues, develop options with clear implications for consideration by the relevant process owners and designated GCF authorities.
Maintain a controlled requirements and dependency framework linking approved process decisions to procedures, tools, system changes, responsible owners, milestones, and implementation status.
B. Specialized Fiduciary Standards Implementation and Case-Based Analysis

Coordinate with Regional Team focal points and other relevant stakeholders to manage the pipeline of programming stage cases requiring fiduciary standards review. Maintain visibility of case status, milestones, dependencies, outstanding actions, and required touchpoints, and facilitate timely information flow and coordination to support orderly pipeline development and review.

Undertake the operational analysis of prioritized programming stage during the interim implementation period to identify recurring process issues, evidence gaps, decision bottlenecks, and improvements required in the emerging operating model.
Maintain a structured case framework capturing the applicable specialized fiduciary functions, evidence references, review outcomes, conditions, unresolved matters, and carry-forward actions.

Synthesize lessons from live cases and stakeholder feedback into reference templates to enable improvements to procedures, reviewer guidance, frequently asked questions, training materials, and system requirements.
Maintain records of feedback, decisions, action owners, and closure status, and escalate matters requiring policy or technical interpretation to the Fiduciary Advisory Principal.
Prepare analytical briefs and management submissions.
C. Systems Integration
Support and coordinate the documentation of business requirements for incorporating specialized fiduciary standards into the GCF Partner Portal and Project Review and Tracking Platform.
Coordinate with business and technology owners to resolve requirements, sequencing, dependencies, testing issues, and migration arrangements, and provide clear advice on readiness for implementation.
Design the transition from interim registers and templates to approved system functionality, including data-quality, ownership, retention, and handover requirements.
D. Stakeholder Consultation, Change Implementation, and Capacity Development

Plan and facilitate structured consultations and technical working sessions with Regional Teams, process owners, the Office of the Chief Investment Officer, the Department of Information Technology, and other relevant stakeholders.

Prepare consultation materials, present proposed operating arrangements, test their usability and control effectiveness, synthesize stakeholder feedback, and recommend how substantive issues should be resolved.
Prepare periodic management reports setting out progress, decisions taken, risks, dependencies, outstanding issues, proposed mitigations, and implementation readiness.
At the end of the assignment, compile a final repository of trackers, registers, decisions, migration records, and implementation documentation for handover to business-as-usual owners.
E. Compliance and Confidentiality
Ensure that all operational activities adhere to applicable internal requirements concerning confidentiality, conflicts of interest, information security, and records management.
Maintain implementation records and correspondence securely and systematically, with appropriate access and version control.
Exercise sound judgement in identifying matters that require escalation and refer to all technical, policy, fiduciary, and system decisions to the designated GCF authority.
Required experience and qualifications
Advanced university degree in business administration, finance, project management, information systems, or another relevant field.

At least five (5) years of relevant professional experience in working in matrix hierarchy structures, managing complex relationships, demonstrative competence in conflict management, institutional process design, business analysis, operational policy implementation, fiduciary or financial operations, programme delivery, or a closely related field.
Proven experience independently analyzing complex processes and translating policy or control requirements into implementable procedures, workflows, tools, and business requirements.

Demonstrated experience coordinating and facilitating cross-functional consultations, supporting the resolution of competing requirements, preparing options and recommendations for senior decision-makers.
Strong experience in business-process mapping, requirements definition, change implementation, document control, risk and dependency management, and preparation of analytical and management reports.
Experience developing or validating digital workflow requirements, user roles, data fields, controls, dashboards, audit trails, testing scenarios, or migration arrangements is highly desirable.
Experience in an international organization, development finance institution, or climate finance environment is desirable.
Solid understanding of GCF operations, programming processes, accreditation arrangements, and partnership model is an advantage.
Excellent written and spoken English is required.
Competencies
Strong organizational and coordination skills, with close attention to detail and record accuracy.
Strong problem-solving and implementation skills.
Excellent drafting, presentation, and management-reporting skills.
Ability to manage multiple workstreams, competing priorities, and tight deadlines under minimal supervision.
Ability to work effectively and collaboratively with diverse stakeholders across teams.
Proactive, solution-oriented, responsive, and able to follow actions through to completion.
Strong analytical judgement and the ability to identify root causes, assess options, and make clear, evidence-based recommendations.
Sound judgement on when issues require escalation.
High standards of professionalism, confidentiality, integrity, and accuracy.
Ability to work outside regular hours when required to accommodate engagement across time zones.
